reason: Real Windows Product Experience UAT at exact candidate 1ab5705ec3ae35221fb78cddad9b6048aff8ad96 failed closed before launch with SOURCE_UAT_ELECTRON_ARCHIVE_HASH_MISMATCH. The expected Windows Electron 39.8.5 SHA-256 d75c0057fd58c08023ff82ed9dd38443f90b4a962c9a9359aa74d9070f4add34 is correct and is also the Git LFS pointer oid. The UAT source archive instead contained the tracked Git LFS pointer bytes themselves; the SHA-256 of that exact pointer text is a761d326fb631ad93feb8113e5c1c6818d62de455afd8688e725d261564feb1b, exactly matching the real Windows failure. The existing Round12/13 identity-bound packager reads Git blobs through git cat-file, which is correct for ordinary blobs but yields LFS pointer text for LFS-tracked archives. This work package authorizes a failure-first repair that reuses the repository's existing mature Git LFS materialization pattern: targeted git lfs pull of the trusted Windows Electron object in Product Final Validation, then package-time detection of Git LFS pointer blobs and strict replacement only with already-materialized worktree bytes whose SHA-256 and size exactly match the pointer oid and size. No new downloader, cache, package manager, release authority, or Yance general-purpose infrastructure is authorized.

evidence.trustedExistingPattern: .github/workflows/reviewed-candidate-a6.yml targeted git lfs pull + SHA256 + size + clean-tree verification
evidence.rootCause: create-round12-13-windows-uat-package.js reads tracked content with git cat-file and therefore serializes Git LFS pointer blobs rather than materialized LFS object bytes into the UAT source ZIP

implementation.matureOssAuthority: git-lfs already used by repository workflows and .gitattributes

mandatoryFailureFirstContracts: A synthetic tracked Git LFS pointer must never be written into the identity-bound UAT ZIP as if it were the real binary payload.

When a tracked Git blob is a Git LFS pointer, package generation must require already-materialized worktree bytes and verify both SHA-256 equals the pointer oid and byte length equals the pointer size before archiving.
If the worktree still contains the pointer text, or materialized bytes do not match pointer oid or size, package generation fails closed before producing a promotable UAT candidate.
Product Final Validation must explicitly materialize only the trusted Windows Electron LFS object before Round12/13 UAT packaging and verify it against release/electron-distribution-trust.json.
The repair must reuse mature Git LFS behavior and must not add a Yance downloader, alternate Electron source, integrity bypass, expected-hash rewrite, or Windows-side recovery download.
